**Top of mind:** Google DeepMind is now run day-to-day by Koray Kavukcuoglu after Demis Hassabis moved up to chairman, and Jeff Dean left Google after 27 years to co-found Discovery Loop — a reshuffle that puts vendor relationships at one of the biggest human-data buyers in play and creates a brand-new science-focused lab to sell into. Meanwhile, Anthropic disclosed a 20-year, $9.1B compute deal with Riot Platforms as part of roughly $71B in compute commitments — a strong signal that frontier training demand, and the data spend that follows it, keeps compounding.

## Competitor moves

- **Fallout continues from Forbes' exposé on US data vendors selling to Chinese labs.** Forbes (Aug 5) reported Mercor booked ~2% of Q2 revenue from Chinese labs on a >$2B annualized run rate, Surge AI CEO Edwin Chen traveled to China to court lab executives, and Turing project documents point to ByteDance work; Micro1 CEO Ali Ansari publicly countered that his firm won't sell data to adversarial nations. Expect labs and Washington to tighten vendor-compliance requirements — a clean geo-compliance posture is becoming a sales weapon. [Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/annatong/2026/08/05/silicon-valleys-other-china-problem-its-training-their-ai/), [TechBuzz](https://www.techbuzz.ai/articles/meet-the-billionaires-selling-ai-its-training-data)
- **Mercor's H1 2026 revenue reportedly passed $615M (~90% from frontier labs); valuation talk at ~$20B, with Surge AI pegged at $25B+.** The Information reports revenue surging at both Mercor and Handshake on demand for human contractors to train AI. The market keeps growing fast, but extreme customer concentration means pricing power sits with a handful of lab buyers — diversification beyond frontier labs is the open flank. [The Information](https://www.theinformation.com/articles/handshake-mercor-revenue-surges-demand-human-contractors-train-ai), [BigGo Finance](https://finance.biggo.com/news/865c23cb-3e0d-4c21-aa0d-6bf2a7fc8d1a), [TechBuzz](https://www.techbuzz.ai/articles/meet-the-billionaires-selling-ai-its-training-data)

## New projects & opportunities

- **River AI raised $1.1B (Aug 11) to help enterprises train, tune, and serve their own models.** xAI co-founder Igor Babuschkin's startup is backed by General Catalyst, AMP PBC, NVIDIA, and AMD Ventures; a wave of enterprise custom-model building means every deployment needs SFT, RLHF, and eval data — a direct services opening below the frontier-lab tier. [AIwire](https://www.hpcwire.com/aiwire/2026/08/11/river-ai-secures-1-1b-to-make-custom-ai-models-easier-to-train-and-deploy/)
- **OpenAI launched GPT-5.6-Cyber for vetted security defenders (Aug 11).** Specialized frontier models in high-stakes domains need scarce domain-expert data and red-team evals; cybersecurity expert sourcing — where India has a deep talent pool — is an underserved, high-rate niche. [Tech Startups](https://techstartups.com/2026/08/11/top-tech-news-today-august-11-2026-anthropic-intel-meta-openai-nvidia-unitree-more/)
- **India angle: Activate AI, a $75M India-focused AI fund (backer of unicorn Sarvam), profiled Aug 11.** More funded Indian model startups means more local demand for Indic-language, domain-specific data and evals — customers who prefer India-based delivery. [Tech Startups](https://techstartups.com/2026/08/11/top-tech-news-today-august-11-2026-anthropic-intel-meta-openai-nvidia-unitree-more/) (orig. Rest of World)
- **Alibaba is releasing Qwen3.8 open weights (reported Aug 10).** Frontier-scale open weights accelerate enterprise fine-tuning, shifting data demand from pre-training scale toward high-quality post-training sets that mid-market clients must buy rather than build. [BuildFastWithAI](https://www.buildfastwithai.com/blogs/ai-news-today-august-10-2026)

## Frontier lab movements

- **Anthropic signed a 20-year, ~$9.1B compute agreement with Riot Platforms (~191MW at Rockdale, TX), part of ~$71B in total compute commitments.** Multi-decade compute buildouts imply years of continued frontier training runs — the core driver of human-data and eval spend. [Tech Startups](https://techstartups.com/2026/08/11/top-tech-news-today-august-11-2026-anthropic-intel-meta-openai-nvidia-unitree-more/)
- **Meta announced a pivot toward open-source AI (Aug 11).** If Meta's frontier work goes open, model differentiation shifts further toward proprietary data and post-training quality — structurally good for data vendors, and worth watching for what it means for Meta-owned Scale AI's lab business. [WBUR](https://www.wbur.org/hereandnow/2026/08/11/meta-open-source-ai)
- **OpenAI is reportedly targeting an IPO as soon as September 2026.** Public-market capital would fund even bigger data programs, but quarterly scrutiny could push labs toward outcome-based pricing and consolidation onto fewer, audited vendors. [BuildFastWithAI](https://www.buildfastwithai.com/blogs/ai-news-today-august-10-2026)

## Research papers

- **SWE-Bench ProMax: an expert-curated, multilingual code-refactoring benchmark (Yuling Shi et al., Aug 10).** 170 instances across seven languages, with issue descriptions rewritten from scratch and test suites manually reviewed; the best frontier model resolves only 41.2%. Takeaway: labs still pay for painstaking human curation, and agentic-coding evals are far from saturated — a concrete, sellable SKU. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09802), [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/papers/2608.09802)
- **Contamination-proof evaluation via adversarial fast-moving real-world domains (William Bolton et al., ICML 2026 AI-for-Science workshop).** Uses 2026 F1 car-design innovations and freshly rotated Magic: The Gathering card pools as post-cutoff ground truth models can't have memorized. The methodology is a template for continuously refreshed eval subscriptions — evals that expire by design create recurring revenue. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03569v1)

## Leadership movements

- **Demis Hassabis stepped back from running Google DeepMind; Koray Kavukcuoglu, a 13-year DeepMind veteran, takes day-to-day control as SVP.** Hassabis becomes chairman and Alphabet chief scientist. New operational leadership at one of the largest data buyers means vendor relationships and procurement priorities are in play — worth refreshing DeepMind contacts now. [Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/08/05/google-deepmind-demis-hassabis-ai), [The Decoder](https://the-decoder.com/google-deepmind-loses-both-its-ceo-and-chief-scientist-as-demis-hassabis-and-jeff-dean-step-down-simultaneously/)
- **Jeff Dean left Google after 27 years to co-found Discovery Loop with Sanjay Ghemawat; Oriol Vinyals and Quoc Le are joining.** The Google-backed public benefit corporation aims to speed up ML-driven discoveries in science and engineering — a brand-new prospective buyer of expert scientific data and evaluation, worth an early BD approach. [The Decoder](https://the-decoder.com/google-deepmind-loses-both-its-ceo-and-chief-scientist-as-demis-hassabis-and-jeff-dean-step-down-simultaneously/), [TNW](https://thenextweb.com/news/google-deepmind-shakeup-hassabis-jeff-dean-vinyals-discovery-loop)
- **Chloé Bakalar, OpenAI's head of ethics, departed less than a year after joining (Aug 11, via FT).** Another senior governance exit at OpenAI amid safety scrutiny — relevant to how labs structure oversight of data-sourcing and human-feedback pipelines, and the compliance bar vendors will be held to. [Tech Startups](https://techstartups.com/2026/08/11/top-tech-news-today-august-11-2026-anthropic-intel-meta-openai-nvidia-unitree-more/)

**Top of mind:** Forbes' investigation into US data vendors quietly selling human-preference data to Chinese labs (Surge AI, Mercor, Turing named) is snowballing into a Washington policy fight over export controls on training data — a potential contract reshuffle that favors vendors with clean China exposure. Meanwhile Google DeepMind's leadership shakeup (Hassabis to chairman, Jeff Dean out after 27 years to found Discovery Loop) signals an even more aggressive frontier race, which means sustained demand for expert data and evals.

## Competitor moves

- **Forbes exposé: Surge AI, Mercor and Turing tied to a ~$500M/yr US-to-China training-data trade.** Tencent, Ant, Alibaba and ByteDance reportedly buy the same human-preference datasets supplied to OpenAI and Anthropic — while Surge and Mercor also hold US government contracts, inviting FOCI/export-control scrutiny. If Washington acts, security-sensitive contracts could migrate to vendors with no China exposure. [Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/annatong/2026/08/05/silicon-valleys-other-china-problem-its-training-their-ai/), [ChinaTalk](https://www.chinatalk.media/p/the-mercor-hack-and-the-commoditization), [AI Weekly](https://aiweekly.co/alerts/surge-ai-mercor-reportedly-sell-training-data-to-chinese-labs)
- **Mercor's breach fallout keeps compounding — at least seven federal lawsuits now filed.** The March supply-chain hack (~4TB including contractor IDs, biometrics and interview videos) has become the industry's cautionary tale on contractor-data security; expect customers to tighten vendor security audits, which is a differentiator for whoever can pass them. [Staffing Industry Analysts](https://www.staffingindustry.com/news/global-daily-news/ai-staffing-firm-mercor-faces-lawsuits-over-data-breach), [PYMNTS](https://www.pymnts.com/legal/2026/ai-startup-mercor-faces-lawsuit-over-data-breach/), [ChinaTalk](https://www.chinatalk.media/p/the-mercor-hack-and-the-commoditization)

## New projects & opportunities

- **EU AI Act Article 10 fully enforced since Aug 2 — annotation and labeling are now regulated data-governance operations for high-risk AI.** Compliance-grade labeling (documented provenance, QA trails, human oversight per Article 14) is becoming a paid requirement, not a nice-to-have — a concrete pitch for vendors who can offer auditable pipelines to EU-exposed customers. [Kili Technology](https://kili-technology.com/blog/best-on-premise-data-labeling-platforms-for-regulated-industries-2026-guide), [Humans in the Loop](https://humansintheloop.org/data-annotation-trends-2026-forecast-best-practices/)
- **China-exposure scrutiny is creating a "neutral vendor" opening.** With US labs and federal buyers now asking who else their data suppliers serve, vendors that can attest to clean customer lists have a new sales wedge for defense- and government-adjacent RLHF/eval work. [Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/annatong/2026/08/05/silicon-valleys-other-china-problem-its-training-their-ai/)

## Frontier lab movements

- **Anthropic disclosed ~$71B in compute commitments and launched the "Theseus" datacenter venture with Macquarie and GIC.** Compute build-outs at this scale telegraph bigger training runs ahead — historically a leading indicator of post-training data and eval spend. [Michael Parekh / RTZ](https://michaelparekh.substack.com/p/ai-weekly-summary-rtz-1004)
- **Meta released Muse Glimmer (Aug 10): a 30B open-weights multimodal model tuned for agentic tool use and LLM-as-judge.** A capable free judge model lowers the cost floor for automated eval — pushing human-data vendors further up-market toward expert adjudication and hard cases. [Price Per Token](https://pricepertoken.com/news/model-releases), [AI Weekly](https://aiweekly.co/ai-news-today)
- **OpenAI's GPT-5.6-Cyber is its first model rated 'High' for cyber capability under the Preparedness Framework.** Crossing capability thresholds forces more red-teaming and safety evaluation — a growing demand line for specialized cyber eval and adversarial data. [Price Per Token](https://pricepertoken.com/news/model-releases)

## Research papers

- **CoT-Core: CoT-aware coreset selection to slash LLM evaluation cost** — Qihua Pan, Zhenheng Tang, Peijie Dong, Xiang Liu et al. Picking small, representative eval subsets that preserve ranking fidelity could change how labs buy eval data: fewer, higher-value items. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.00014)
- **Agentic Coding in the Wild: GitHub Copilot traces at production scale** — Banruo Liu, Haoran Qiu, Íñigo Goiri, Rodrigo Fonseca, Ricardo Bianchini, Esha Choukse (Microsoft). Production agent-trace datasets show where coding agents fail — a map of exactly the failure modes labs will pay human experts to annotate and repair. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.00101)
- **Can LLM Agents Price Competitively? A dynamic multi-attribute auction benchmark for agentic commerce** — Shimaa Ahmed, Yiwei Cai, Mohsen Minaei, Rahul Rachuri. New agentic-commerce benchmarks mean new eval-harness and scenario-authoring work as labs chase agent reliability in transactions. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.00102)

- **Demis Hassabis stepped back from running Google DeepMind (Aug 5); Koray Kavukcuoglu takes day-to-day control and the Gemini roadmap.** Hassabis becomes DeepMind chairman and Alphabet chief scientist; a Kavukcuoglu-led, ship-faster DeepMind likely means more post-training and eval cycles. [Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/08/05/google-deepmind-demis-hassabis-ai), [The Decoder](https://the-decoder.com/google-deepmind-loses-both-its-ceo-and-chief-scientist-as-demis-hassabis-and-jeff-dean-step-down-simultaneously/)

Alphabet shed roughly $160-200B in market value on the news. [Quartz](https://qz.com/jeff-dean-google-chief-scientist-discovery-loop-startup-080526), [HNGN](https://www.hngn.com/articles/272649/20260808/google-chief-scientist-jeff-dean-departs-after-27-years-launch-new-discovery-loop-startup.htm)

Meanwhile the fallout continues from two Aug 5 bombshells: Google DeepMind's leadership shakeup (Hassabis stepping back, Jeff Dean and three other legends leaving to found Discovery Loop) and Forbes' exposé that Surge AI, Mercor and peers are quietly selling training data to Chinese labs — a story that puts vendor neutrality and compliance at the center of every lab's procurement conversation.

[Seoul Economic Daily](https://en.sedaily.com/finance/2026/08/07/even-a-legend-departs-google-reorganizes-as-it-falls-behind), [Memeburn](https://memeburn.com/google-deepmind-brain-drain-2026/)

## Research papers

- **LongHorizon-Harness: Advancing Long-Horizon Agents for Real-World Tasks (AMAP-ML, Alibaba).** A new August harness/benchmark for evaluating agents on long-horizon real-world tasks — a direct blueprint for the agentic-evaluation data products labs are currently buying; worth mining for task taxonomies and rubric design. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24653), [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/papers/2607.24653)

A concrete new line item to pitch, and cyber/security talent is a pool Indian vendors can staff quickly. [OpenAI](https://openai.com/index/responding-next-frontier-critical-cyber-capabilities/), [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/07/openai-says-it-slowed-astra-model-development-over-security-concerns/)

## Frontier lab movements

- **OpenAI slowed work on Astra over security concerns (Aug 7).** An internal review found the unreleased model made significant advances in agentic coding and cybersecurity, crossing the threshold at which it could independently identify and execute attacks on well-protected systems; fallout coverage continued through Aug 8. Expect rivals to face the same bar — and to buy the evals that prove where their models stand. [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/07/openai-says-it-slowed-astra-model-development-over-security-concerns/), [OpenAI](https://openai.com/index/responding-next-frontier-critical-cyber-capabilities/)
- **Anthropic confirmed an in-house chip-design team (Aug 5), targeting ~50% lower per-token inference cost.** The hardware–software co-design effort is anchored by Clive Chan (ex-OpenAI chip team, ex-Tesla Dojo), with Samsung reported as manufacturing partner, alongside its existing Nvidia/AMD/TPU/Trainium stack. Cheaper inference frees budget for the post-training data and evaluation spend where models actually differentiate — and signals Anthropic is planning for sustained training scale. [Quartz](https://qz.com/anthropic-custom-ai-chip-design-team-claude-080526), [Tom's Hardware](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/anthropic-to-build-its-own-co-designed-custom-ai-accelerator-for-inferencing-workloads-samsung-reported-to-be-partnering-with-the-claude-ai-maker-for-manufacturing), [Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/jonmarkman/2026/08/06/anthropic-enters-the-ai-chip-race-with-in-house-chip-team/)

## Research papers

- **Adaptive allocation of human-evaluation budgets (Zouhar et al., posted to arXiv early August).** Vilém Zouhar, Julia Kreutzer, Alon Lavie, Tom Kocmi, Matt Post, Ondřej Bojar, and Mrinmaya Sachan formalize multi-model human evaluation as best-arm identification in a multi-armed bandit: sampling adaptively on interim rankings concentrates annotator budget on the most competitive models, making evals faster and cheaper at the same discriminative power. Worth folding into eval delivery now — adaptive sampling protects margins as clients squeeze eval budgets, and it's a methodology differentiator in proposals. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03437)

## New projects & opportunities

- **The US frontier-eval framework is done — and classified, which creates a prep market.** The White House confirmed the voluntary framework from the June EO was completed by its Aug 1 deadline: classified benchmarks, secret thresholds, and a ~30-day pre-release government access window administered by NIST's CAISI; OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic reviewed a draft, and open-weight models are reportedly excluded. Labs must now prep models for tests they can't see — that means demand for proxy evals, adversarial red-teaming, and cyber-capability test sets from outside vendors. ## Research papers

- **LongHorizon-Harness: move task-state tracking outside the model, verify against the environment (AMAP-ML, Alibaba — Aug 3).** A Manage-Execute-Audit loop with a read-only auditor lifts Terminal-Bench 2.1 from 69.7% to 77.2% and OSWorld 2.0 from 2.8% to 8.3% (Qwen 3.7-Plus), with gains across models. Verification-heavy harness design is exactly the kind of work labs outsource: human-verified environment states, audit rubrics, and failure-mode annotation. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01964), [HF Papers](https://huggingface.co/papers/2608.01964), [GitHub](https://github.com/AMAP-ML/LongHorizon-Harness)
- **OSReward: VLM judges of computer-use agents are systematically too lenient — human annotation still wins (HKU NLP / OS-Copilot — Jul 30).** The benchmark finds even frontier judges mislabel failed runs as successes; the team releases OS-Shepherd-100K (human reasoning-annotated trajectory judgments) and open 9B/35B reward models that match commercial judges at 30–60% lower cost. Double-edged for the industry: strong sales evidence for multi-stage human QC on agent-trajectory data now, and a preview of cheap auto-grading later — worth adopting internally before clients use it to push rates down. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28609), [Project page](https://os-copilot.github.io/OSReward-Home/), [HF Papers](https://huggingface.co/papers/2607.28609)
